method:
# Feature Guide

A Feature describes one coherent capability that a BA hands to the team for breakdown into PBIs. It defines business rules (BRs) that PBIs reference and Acceptance Criteria verify.

## Guiding principle

- The Feature decides behaviour; PBIs implement slices of it. Anything a developer would otherwise have to guess must be decided here or flagged.
- Number every business rule (BR01, BR02 …) so PBIs and ACs can reference it.
- Never invent a behavioural decision silently — flag it in Open Questions / Risks with a proposed default.

## Sections

1. **User Story** — As a [role], I want to [action], so that [outcome].
2. **Description** — context and the problem being solved, in a short paragraph or two.
3. **Roles** — list the roles, or a permission matrix (markdown table) when actions are gated differently per role.
4. **Business Rules** — one Entry per rule: title = "BRnn - Short name", body = the rule stated precisely, including edge cases.
5. **Scope** — Entries titled "In scope" or "Out of scope"; give the reason for out-of-scope items.
6. **Open Questions / Risks** — one Entry per question: title = "N. Question"; body lines "Why it matters:", "Proposed default:", "Tagged to:", "Status:".
7. **Dependencies** — known facts that must exist before delivery (APIs, other Features, external parties).
8. **Design** — Figma link(s), or N/A with a reason.
9. **Acceptance Criteria** — one Entry per scenario: title = "ACnn - Name (ref: BRnn)", body in Given / When / Then. ACs verify BRs; they never introduce new decisions.

## Working process

1. Grill the requirement until each rule is precise enough to test.
2. Use Glossary terms exactly; propose new terms when language is fuzzy.
3. Unresolved branches go to Open Questions / Risks with a proposed default.
